Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

Isoformic 0.1.3 (Development Version)

Release Date: Unreleased

Development Changelog: dev

This release rebuilds the package around the IsoformicExperiment class. Table-based helpers remain available as data-frame methods, but every analysis and plot is now first a method on the object.

Added

  • IsoformicExperiment is an S7 class modelled after SummarizedExperiment with three consistent levels: transcript assays, gene assays (derived by summing isoforms, cached, overridable with gene_assays<-) and exon structures from the annotation. Properties are validated on every change.
  • Annotation is stored on disk as a directory of Parquet files written by DuckDB (prepare_isoformic_annotation(), with n_exons, tx_length, metadata and sequence region tables). The parser is vocabulary-agnostic: besides GENCODE GFF3/GTF it reads Ensembl and Ensembl Rapid Release GFF3, NCBI RefSeq GFF3 and the T2T-CHM13 Liftoff/CAT annotations, keeping the source_gene/source_transcript attributes of lifted annotations as source_gene_id/source_transcript_id columns.
  • download_reference() covers Ensembl (any release, species and division, including Ensembl Plants/Metazoa/Fungi/Protists), any NCBI assembly by accession, T2T-CHM13v2.0 (reference = "t2t") and MANE releases; download_reference_url() caches any file by URL and download_hprc_annotation() fetches the HPRC per-haplotype CAT annotations.
  • Annotation tables carry transcript tags and an is_canonical flag (MANE Select, Ensembl canonical, RefSeq Select), used by dominant_isoform() to report dominant_is_canonical.
  • Haplotype-resolved annotations: prepare_isoformic_annotation(haplotype = ) labels one haplotype, merge_annotations() combines per-haplotype files (HPRC CAT, trio-binned assemblies) into one annotation directory with unique identifiers, and haplotype_summary() reports per-gene haplotype fractions and dominant-isoform switches between haplotypes.
  • FANTOM CAT / FANTOM6 support: download_reference(reference = "fantom") fetches a FANTOM CAT level (GTF), download_fantom_cat_tables() the companion tables, and the parser keeps geneClass (as gene and fallback transcript type), geneCategory, DHS_type, coding_status, cumulative_support and TIEScore; add_fantom_cat_tables() attaches CAGE cluster promoters and the gene information table.
  • Per-transcript structure: the parser aggregates CDS features (cds_start, cds_end, cds_length) and keeps transcript_support_level; transcript_features() computes ORF and UTR lengths, the 50-nt NMD rule (stop_to_last_junction, nmd_predicted), transcription start/end groups (alternative promoters and 3’ ends), the canonical isoform of each gene and splicing events relative to it (splicing_events(): skipped and novel exons, retained introns, alternative splice sites, first and last exons).
  • Productivity as a graded, computed property: transcript_productivity() (productive, altered_productive, unproductive, noncoding, uncertain, with the reason for each call), productive_fraction() per sample or group with the between-group change, run_productivity_enrichment() (gene sets ranked by change in productive fraction), poison_exons() and highlight_poison_exons in plot_genomic_context().
  • add_annotation_columns() attaches external per-transcript or per-gene evidence (Ribo-seq, NMD inhibition, GTEx dominant isoforms, domain retention, …) to the annotation; a productivity_evidence column overrides the computed productivity.
  • Transcript sequences: extract_transcript_sequences() stores the spliced sequence of every transcript in the annotation directory (annot_data_sequences.parquet), from a genome FASTA (streamed in chunks, gzip or plain, chromosome names matched with or without chr) or a transcript FASTA; has_sequences() and transcript_sequences() read it.
  • Sequence-aware ORFs: transcript_orfs() projects the canonical start codon of each gene onto every isoform and translates it (the ORFanage approach), so novel transcripts without CDS get an ORF; annotated CDS are re-read from the sequence (annotation_cds_agrees), with stop codon, genomic coordinates, uORFs, frame relative to the canonical ORF and an NMD class (ptc, ptc_start_proximal, non_stop, long_3utr, none). coding_potential() scores the longest ORF with the Fickett statistic, an in-frame hexamer score and a frozen logistic model trained on GENCODE 50 (build_coding_model(), data-raw/build_coding_model.R; 9,938 coding and 10,000 non-coding transcripts, held-out sensitivity 0.941 and specificity 0.919 at the 0.364 cutoff, AUC 0.978).
  • transcript_productivity() uses the sequence-derived ORFs when present (use_sequence), reports source (sequence, annotation, evidence), distinguishes alternative starts, in-frame changes, frameshifts and stops in novel sequence among altered_productive isoforms, calls non-stop decay and start-proximal stops, and applies evidence columns in a fixed priority (productivity_evidence, validated NMD exon, Ribo-seq main ORF, APPRIS principal).
  • Frozen evidence datasets (frozen_datasets(), fetch_frozen_data(), read_frozen_data(), build_frozen_*()): APPRIS principal isoforms and method scores plus SPADE Pfam domain coordinates (e116v50, Ensembl 116 / GENCODE 50), GENCODE Ribo-seq ORFs phase 1 and 2, NMD-inducing exons validated by NMD inhibition (Karousis et al. 2021), the PolyASite 2.0 atlas and GTEx v8 median transcript TPM per tissue. Files are pinned by version and MD5, downloaded from the first mirror that has them (frozen_mirrors(): user option, the frozen-data GitHub release, the Zenodo snapshot of the processed files) or rebuilt from the sources; bundle_frozen_data() assembles the Zenodo deposit and data-raw/README.md documents the update and deposit procedure.
  • New article “What makes an isoform hard to quantify?”: three samples quantified with 30 and 100 Gibbs draws, and how transcript type, reads, length, exons, isoforms in the gene, GC content, MANE and support tags, NAGNAG and nearby alternative splice sites, unique exonic bases, the closest sibling and unique fragments relate to the inferential uncertainty, to how reliably 30 draws measure it, and to the stability of TreeTerminus trees. The tables come from data-raw/knockdown/isoform_features.R and ship in inst/extdata/knockdown/stability/.
  • New article “Is quantification uncertainty worth checking? Genome-wide evidence”: an evaluation pre-registered for a placenta cohort (control-versus-control null splits and held-out halves of the samples; data-raw/uncertainty_evidence/, prereg.yaml with its amendments), with two checks added outside the plan: mouse control-versus-control comparisons (amendment A19) and technical read halves of two knockdown series. Negative results are included. With 7 versus 7 samples no excess of false positives from ignoring the inferential uncertainty was detected (rate ratio 1.00; the conservative raw jackknife interval, 0.56 to 1.76, does not rule one out). The excess with 3 or 5 samples per group held only at p < 0.01, not at the FDR level, and the second pre-registered result is fragile once genes are treated as clusters. An unstable direction (sign_agreement below 0.95; a secondary flag of the analysis scripts, with only its 0.95 threshold in the plan, made the headline after the results, one cohort, edgeR calls) predicted non-replication in held-out halves of the placenta cohort (odds ratio 0.36, gene-clustered interval 0.31 to 0.41; lower raw replication in all 60 directed pairs of halves) but found only about 10% of the calls that did not replicate. The uncertainty defaults now follow this article (see Changed).
  • read_treeterminus() reads the transcript trees of TreeTerminus (Newick; leaves are positions in quant.sf, named from a Salmon directory) and cut_transcript_trees() cuts them where the inferential relative variance of the summed replicates falls below the cutoff: an isoform the reads determine stays itself, one they do not is replaced by its lowest well-determined ancestor, and nested choices are merged so that the groups never overlap. The groups go to add_uncertainty(groups = ), so ambiguous and collapse_groups work at the resolution the data support, isoform by isoform. Tested on real TreeTerminus output.
  • run_terminus() runs Terminus from R (terminus group on every Salmon directory, then the consensus terminus collapse) through condathis, checks first that every directory has replicates and equivalence-class weights, deletes the multi-gigabyte delta.log of each sample as soon as it is grouped, and returns the consensus groups. On the six GSE129540 samples it reproduces the consensus of the command-line run.
  • read_terminus_groups() reads the transcript groups of Terminus (terminus collapse, clusters.txt), and add_uncertainty(groups = ) accepts them (or any table of transcript_id and group_id) in place of the groups built from the correlation of the replicates; ambiguous, collapse_groups and uncertainty_methods() follow the new groups. The parser is tested on real output of Terminus 0.1.0 on Salmon 2.8.0.
  • test_usage() tests differential transcript usage with edgeR diffSplice, satuRn or DEXSeq (all in Suggests) on counts divided by the overdispersion of the replicates, and reports transcript and gene level p-values in one layout. With more than two groups it tests every level against the first, every pair (contrasts = "pairwise") or a list of c(numerator, denominator) pairs, and stacks the results with a contrast column; diffSplice and satuRn fit all groups once, DEXSeq fits each pair. contrasts = "omnibus" tests for a difference among any of the groups: the DEXSeq likelihood-ratio test on all samples, or the Simes combination of the contrasts against the reference for diffSplice and satuRn. Its workers (forked BiocParallel workers for satuRn and DEXSeq, default 1) accepts "auto" and is checked like the workers of run_enrichment(); it does not read the isoformic.workers option.
  • read_oarfish_sc() reads the single-cell output of Oarfish (--single-cell: .count.mtx, .barcodes.txt, .features.txt) and sums the cells of each sample, given a table of barcodes and samples, into an IsoformicExperiment (pseudobulk; TPM from the annotated transcript lengths). read_oarfish_sc_counts() returns the cell-level counts as a long table. The fixture is real Oarfish 0.10.3 output on simulated barcoded reads.
  • read_oarfish() reads long-read quantifications from Oarfish (counts, lengths, TPM computed from them). read_inferential_replicates(), equivalence_support() (from the unique and ambiguous read counts), salmon_run_qc() and add_uncertainty() accept Oarfish output prefixes, including the Parquet bootstrap replicates (.infreps.pq). The bundled fixture is real Oarfish 0.10.3 output on simulated nanopore reads. Mixing Oarfish and Salmon in one call is an error (isoformic_mixed_quantifiers).
  • inferential_overdispersion() and scale_counts() put the quantification uncertainty into the counts as edgeR::catchSalmon() does (Baldoni et al. 2024). add_uncertainty() keeps only the replicates of the transcripts with a mean count of at least min_count, but read_inferential_replicates() records the mean and variance of the replicates of every transcript (moments attribute), and the prior and the estimates come from them: on six GSE129540 samples with 68,245 of 517,038 transcripts kept (min_count = 5), every estimate matches catchSalmon() (largest relative difference 4e-12), and the prior is 1.61, where the kept transcripts alone would give 5.23. A read-split experiment on GSE129540 (data-raw/knockdown/validate_uncertainty.R) checks the uncertainty columns against technical replication: the isoforms called in one half of the reads reproduce in the other half less often as the inferential variance rises. Between read halves every flag predicts non-replication, so this supports the information in the draws, not one flag in particular. The small result tables are bundled and shown in the uncertainty article.
  • Splice-site strength without an external model. extract_splice_sites() (and extract_transcript_sequences() when given a genome FASTA) store the donor and acceptor windows of every intron in the annotation directory (annot_data_splice_sites.parquet); splice_site_strength() scores them with position weight matrices trained on the introns of the canonical transcripts of the same annotation and reports weakest_donor and weakest_acceptor per transcript, or the scores per intron. On GENCODE 50 (698,612 introns) the extraction takes about 1.5 minutes and the scoring 25 s. The scores describe the sites; on their own they separate NMD from protein coding transcripts only slightly (AUC 0.55), so they are evidence to read next to transcript_productivity(), not a classifier.
  • More evidence in the uncertainty tables, none of which changes a default result. isoform_ambiguity() has collapse_gain, the score Terminus groups on (inferential relative variance of the sum of two isoforms minus the mean of their own; negative when the sum is better determined). tx_uncertainty() has low_information, TRUE for an uncertain isoform without a single fragment of its own (the selection of mmcollapse), when equivalence classes were read. add_uncertainty(cor_cutoff = "adaptive") derives the correlation cutoff from the data as mmcollapse does; the default stays -0.5, and on the six GSE129540 samples the adaptive value is -0.25, which calls 36,910 isoforms ambiguous in place of 8,076.
  • equivalence_identifiability() reports which transcripts the equivalence classes of Salmon can tell apart: a transcript is identifiable when its abundance is fixed once the total of every class is fixed. It is a property of the observed classes, not of the posterior draws, and close to independent of them. On the six GSE129540 samples 13,790 of 116,389 expressed isoforms are non-identifiable in every sample, and their estimates differ more between two halves of the reads (median absolute log2 ratio 2.4 against 0.7 at 20 to 100 reads). Takes half a minute to three minutes per human sample and needs Matrix (new in Suggests) for the largest block of transcripts.
  • add_uncertainty(identifiability = TRUE) runs it and adds identifiable and identifiable_fraction to tx_uncertainty(); the table of equivalence_identifiability() can be passed in its place. de_confidence() then reports identifiable (and the flag not identifiable from the equivalence classes). Off by default, so existing results do not change. uncertainty_methods() describes it as a check on class membership, related to but not the same as the non-identifiability of Zheng et al. 2022, which is defined through ranges of optimal estimates.
  • transcript_productivity() treats the GENCODE biotype protein_coding_LoF (148 transcripts in release 50) as unproductive when use_biotype = TRUE: a variant of the reference genome stops its translation.
  • Inferential replicates convert to and from a long table (inferential_replicates_table(), as_inferential_replicates()), and the bundled draws are Parquet tables instead of .rds files. Their moments convert in the same way (inferential_moments_table(), the moments argument of as_inferential_replicates()).
  • Real ESRP knockdown examples for the uncertainty article: GSE129540 (prostate cancer, ESRP2 siRNA) and GSE75489 (H358 cells, ESRP1/2 shRNA), re-quantified with Salmon 2.8.0 and 30 Gibbs draws, reduced to 39 genes (about 1.1 MB). data-raw/knockdown/quantify_knockdown.sh and data-raw/build_knockdown_example.R rebuild them. add_uncertainty() scales the counts with the library_size column of col_data() when present (for objects holding a subset of the transcripts) and accepts the table of equivalence_support() in equivalence.
  • Quantification uncertainty from Salmon: read_inferential_replicates(), equivalence_support() and salmon_run_qc() read the Gibbs/bootstrap replicates, the equivalence classes and the run metadata; add_uncertainty() (or read_salmon(inferential = TRUE)) stores, per transcript, the inferential relative variance, the correlation with the isoforms of the same gene (ambiguity groups that cannot be told apart) and the share of uniquely mapping fragments. de_confidence() repeats a contrast on every draw and reports the interval of the fold-change and the share of draws that agree on its direction (sign_agreement), with unstable flagging a direction that fewer than 95% of the draws agree on, optionally testing ambiguous isoforms as one feature. uncertainty_report() and uncertainty_methods() summarise the results and the settings for a manuscript; plot_de_confidence(), plot_isoform_correlation() and plot_inf_rv() draw them. isoform_switches() counts the significant isoforms with an unstable direction (n_det_unstable) and drop_unstable = TRUE leaves them out; dominant_isoform() and productive_fraction() use the tables too. The tables are written by write_isoformic(), and so are the draws (see below).
  • The documentation site is split into an introduction, a preprocessing article and one article per analysis (diversity, productivity, polyadenylation, enrichment, plots), plus articles on other annotations and on the table-based functions.
  • ?isoformic-options documents every option and environment variable the package reads or is affected by: the isoformic.duckdb_threads, isoformic.duckdb_memory_limit, isoformic.frozen_mirrors, isoformic.orf_cache and isoformic.workers options, the base R download options, the cache location variables and the settings of DuckDB, mirai, parallelly and condathis.
  • options(isoformic.duckdb_threads = , isoformic.duckdb_memory_limit = ) bound the threads and the memory of the DuckDB connections that read and write Parquet and run the annotation queries. When they are unset, the connections follow a Slurm job (SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK, SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE, SLURM_MEM_PER_CPU) and the CPU affinity mask (taskset), which DuckDB does not detect on its own, instead of using every core and 80% of the RAM of the node; a cgroup CPU quota or memory limit below the Slurm allocation still applies. Invalid values (including a memory limit below 1 MiB) raise an error that names the option.
  • run_enrichment(), run_productivity_enrichment() and run_apa_enrichment() gain workers (default: the isoformic.workers option, or 1): above 1 their fgsea calls, one per gene set collection and transcript category, run in parallel on mirai daemons (mirai in Suggests). The daemons receive only the ranking of their call and the gene sets cut down to it, so their memory does not grow with the session, unlike forked workers (nproc, BiocParallel::MulticoreParam()), which tools that sum resident memory count once per worker. workers = "auto" uses parallelly::availableCores() (parallelly in Suggests; without it, one worker) and so follows a Slurm allocation, the CPU affinity mask and a cgroup quota. With one worker the results are those of earlier versions; above one every call gets its own seed, drawn from the session’s stream, so the result does not depend on the number of workers but its sampled p-values differ slightly from a serial run. Warnings of fgsea raised on a worker are raised again in the session, naming the collection and the category. The daemons are started on first use, with the session’s library paths and one thread each, and kept for the session, so a loop of small calls does not start them every time; the new isoformic_workers() starts a set number of them ahead or stops them (isoformic_workers(0)), and they also stop when the session ends. Results do not depend on whether the daemons were already running. Daemons that died (for example killed for their memory) are replaced by the next call, and a call whose daemons all die fails instead of waiting forever. Daemons started with mirai::daemons(n, .compute = "isoformic") are used as they are. mirai 2.3.0 or later is needed.
  • Evidence joins: add_appris(), add_riboseq_orfs() (listed transcripts and exon-block compatibility, riboseq_main_orf, riboseq_uorf), add_nmd_exons(), domain_retention() (domains retained, partial or lost relative to the canonical isoform, projected onto novel isoforms) and gtex_reference() / gtex_tissues() (healthy-tissue productive fraction and dominant isoform per gene).
  • Productivity statistics: productivity_fractions() (expression share per class and unproductive mechanism: NMD, retained intron, no ORF, non-stop), test_productive_fraction() (quasi-binomial two-group test on counts), productive_fraction(min_expr = , inf_reps = , reference = ) (expression floor, uncertainty from Salmon inferential replicates, difference to the GTEx baseline), dominant_isoform(min_expr = ) and benchmark_productivity() (recall of NMD and retained-intron biotypes by the rules alone, productive rate of coding and canonical transcripts).
  • Alternative polyadenylation: polya_sites() ranks the 3’ ends of each gene, classifies tandem_utr, alternative_last_exon and intronic events relative to the canonical isoform, finds poly(A) signal hexamers in the sequence and validates ends against the PolyASite atlas or the GENCODE poly(A) GFF (download_reference(file_type = "polya"), read_polya_gff()); apa_usage() quantifies distal usage and weighted 3’ UTR length per sample or group and test_apa() tests the shift.
  • run_apa_enrichment() runs a gene set enrichment analysis on the genes ranked by their change in distal 3’ end usage (rank_by = "delta") or in weighted 3’ UTR length ("utr3_length"), from an object or from the table of apa_usage().
  • Long-read and assembled transcript catalogs: StringTie/Bambu/FLAIR style GTF attributes (reference_id, ref_gene_id, ref_gene_name) are kept, and add_sqanti_classification() writes SQANTI3 structural categories into transcript_type; tx_type_palette() includes those categories and the unknown/novel labels. Tables are read on first use and cached keyed by file signature, so objects sharing an annotation share one copy.
  • Experiments persist as Parquet directories: write_isoformic() and read_isoformic() (optionally self-contained with copy_annotation = TRUE). The inferential replicates in metadata$inf_reps are written to inf_reps/, one wide Parquet file per draw, with their type and moments, and restored as they were (other properties, such as names of the draws, are dropped with a warning). One draw is written and read at a time, so the long table of inferential_replicates_table() (several times the memory of the draws) is no longer needed to keep them. Directories written before have no inf_reps/ and are read without replicates. An object read back now has its draws, so productive_fraction(), test_usage() and uncertainty_report() use them as they do on the original object; to save without them, use add_uncertainty(keep_draws = FALSE) or set x@metadata$inf_reps to NULL before writing.
  • Readers: read_salmon() reads quant.sf files straight into an IsoformicExperiment with DuckDB; read_parquet(), write_parquet() and read_tabular() are exported; make_tx_to_gene() parses FASTA headers with DuckDB and also accepts GFF3/GTF files and annotation directories.
  • SummarizedExperiment-style accessors: tx_assays(), tx_assay(), tx_assay<-, assay_names(), gene_assays(), gene_assay(), gene_data(), gene_names(), row_names(), col_names(), col_data<-, exon_table(), annot_metadata(), clear_cache(), plus dim(), dimnames() and [.
  • Differential expression results are standardised on assignment (de_tx<-, de_gene<- accept DESeq2, edgeR, limma and fishpond column names) and flagged with stored cutoffs (de_cutoffs(), de_cutoffs<-, de_table()).
  • Transcriptomic diversity summaries: isoform_fraction(), tx_diversity() (expressed isoforms, dominant isoform, effective number of isoforms), dominant_isoform() (per group, with dominance switches), isoform_switches() (transcript versus gene level calls) and exon_diversity() (constitutive versus alternative exons).
  • as_summarized_experiment() converts back to SummarizedExperiment at the transcript or gene level; as_isoformic() also accepts tximport lists.
  • example_isoformic() loads a bundled experiment (preeclampsia placenta subset, GENCODE v50) used by all examples and tests.
  • profile_data() and plot_tx_expr() methods for the object; plot_enrichment() and read_gmt().
  • summarize_to_gene() is exported and sums isoforms (abundance-weighted mean for length assays, as tximport does).
  • Case study articles built from complete public datasets: chronic stress in the male mouse adBNST (PRJNA984605, Salmon and swish with batch adjustment) and a CLK inhibitor in prostate cancer cells sequenced with Oxford Nanopore long reads (GSE259334, Oarfish and swish on the bootstrap replicates) (#12). The processed bundles live in vignettes/articles/data/ (not installed) and are rebuilt from the SRA reads by the scripts in data-raw/case_studies/.
  • The articles cite the isoformic paper (#24, #25) and inst/CITATION carries its DOI.

Changed

  • Breaking (development version only; no release had these functions): the uncertainty defaults now follow the genome-wide evaluation in the article “Is quantification uncertainty worth checking? Genome-wide evidence” (see Added). de_confidence() no longer assigns a high/moderate/low confidence class. In a placenta cohort the class marked 83% of the calls (a filter on it would have removed 81% of the calls that replicated), separated replicating from non-replicating calls only modestly once count and test statistic were accounted for (odds ratio 0.68), and in control-versus-control comparisons keeping only its high class removed no more false calls than dropping as many of the least expressed transcripts. The columns confidence and confident_de are removed; unstable (sign_agreement below min_agreement, 0.95) and unstable_de (a significant call with an unstable direction) are added, and reason is renamed flags. Calls with an unstable direction replicated less often in held-out halves of that cohort (odds ratio 0.36; a secondary flag chosen as the headline after the results, one cohort), but the flag found only about 10% of the calls that did not replicate, so a stable direction is not a sign that a call is right. isoform_switches(confident_only = ) is defunct, also as the third positional argument; drop_unstable = TRUE (by name) leaves out the unstable calls, members of a collapsed group included, and n_det_unstable replaces n_det_confident. Without group, de_confidence(min_agreement = , inf_rv_cutoff = ) applies the new thresholds to the stored table, and its n_det_sig and unstable_de follow the current de_tx() results; min_agreement and inf_rv_cutoff must be a single number in range there and in add_uncertainty(), or they raise an error. A feature below min_count has a missing mean_inf_rv in de_confidence(), as in tx_uncertainty(), and is never flagged as “uncertain quantification”. uncertainty_report()$switches needs only the transcript-level table: it is no longer NULL without a gene-level table (its n_det_not_deg is then NA) or without the stored fold-change stability (its “without unstable directions” row is then NA). uncertainty_report()$de counts the significant features per flag (a collapsed group once), with the rule of the ambiguity groups that were used, uncertainty_methods() describes the sign agreement instead of the classes, plot_de_confidence() colours isoforms by the direction over the replicates, and confidence_palette() is removed. inf_rv_cutoff (0.5) and cor_cutoff (-0.5) keep their values but no longer judge a call: an InfRV of at least 0.5 marked 87% of the expressed isoforms of that cohort. read_isoformic() upgrades fold-change tables written by earlier development versions.
  • Breaking (development version only; no release had these functions): the transcript-level accessors are renamed to tx_assay(), tx_assays() and tx_assay<- (matching gene_assay()), so that they no longer mask SummarizedExperiment::assay() and related generics when both packages are attached. The old names assay(), assays() and assay<- are removed.
  • Printing an IsoformicExperiment shows its directory relative to the working directory when it lies under it (the stored path stays absolute).
  • run_enrichment() applies min_size and max_size to the number of genes of a set that have a ranked transcript of the category, as documented, rather than to its number of transcripts. Large sets that were dropped because their genes have many transcripts (about half of the Reactome sets for protein-coding transcripts on GENCODE 50, and hallmark sets such as E2F targets and G2M checkpoint) are now tested, so results change for large sets.
  • polya_signal_distance of polya_sites() is the distance of the occurrence of the hexamer closest to the 3’ end, including one that overlaps an earlier occurrence (as in AATAAAATAAA); such signals were missed before, so the distance can get smaller (about 1.6% of GENCODE 50 transcripts with a signal).
  • polya_sites() reads only the last signal_window nucleotides of each sequence and is cached in the object, so apa_usage(), test_apa() and run_apa_enrichment() reuse it.
  • equivalence_support() sums the equivalence classes in DuckDB and equivalence_identifiability() parses them as numbers, one sample at a time: both use a fraction of the memory and time they did.
  • add_uncertainty(group = ) computes the median, interval and standard deviation of the fold-changes of all features at once, and as_inferential_replicates() builds the draws of a table in the order of inferential_replicates_table() without indexing the whole table.
  • salmon_quant() draws 30 Gibbs samples by default (it was 100; num_gibbs = 0 skips them).
  • salmon_index() and salmon_quant() target Salmon 2 (the Rust rewrite; the conda environment installs 2.8.0): options that Salmon 2 ignores (--no-version-check, --type puff, --disableChainingHeuristic, --useVBOpt) are no longer passed, single-end reads are passed with --unmatedReads, and the documentation explains that indices built with Salmon 1.x must be rebuilt.
  • add_uncertainty() reports when the replicates give fewer than 60 degrees of freedom over the study (samples x (replicates - 1); Baldoni, Chen and Smyth 2024), the number is stored and stated by uncertainty_methods(), and uncertainty_report() has a new replicates table (replicate type, draws, degrees of freedom, median overdispersion).
  • The documentation calls the correlation rule of add_uncertainty() “ambiguity between isoforms” instead of “identifiability”, credits mmcollapse (Turro et al. 2014) and states what the replicates do not measure: non-identifiable abundances (Zheng et al. 2022) and estimates that are wrong because the annotation is incomplete (Ma and Kingsford 2019).
  • plot_genomic_context() is a pure ggplot2 implementation reading the exon table of the annotation (one row per transcript, introns with strand arrows, expression labels and highlighted differentially expressed isoforms); it no longer needs plotgardener, txdbmaker, TxDb, OrgDb or BSgenome packages. plot_tx_context() is now an alias of its data frame method and accepts the legacy column names.
  • plot_genomic_context() labels each transcript on the y axis, aligned with its track (the labels floated above the tracks and overlapped transcripts starting at the left edge), and prints expression labels without padded zeros. As a plain ggplot2 object it renders the same on every graphics device, including Cairo and the RStudio plot panel (#21).
  • plot_log2fc() facets several genes, orders the gene bar first and uses a common theme; plot_log2FC() is kept as a wrapper.
  • plot_tx_expr() and run_enrichment() are S7 generics whose first argument is the object (or a table); run_enrichment() no longer takes the unused lfc_cutoff argument and expands gene sets with a single join.
  • prepare_profile_data() returns the same long table as profile_data() (feature_name, feature_type, gene_name, group, mean_expr, sd_expr, is_de); gene expression is the sum of the isoforms (it was the mean).
  • prepare_annotation() and prepare_exon_annotation() read the Parquet annotation directory and return standard column names (transcript_id, start_pos, end_pos, …).
  • The bundled example data are rebuilt as Parquet: example_isoformic() and the files under system.file("extdata", package = "isoformic") replace the CSV tables of 0.1.2 (see Removed).
  • download_reference() discovers files by listing the release directory on the server instead of relying on hard-coded file names, so any current or future GENCODE release (and genome patch, e.g. GRCh38.p15) works. New region argument ("all", "chr", "primary") selects the annotation flavour; versions are normalised (49, "v49", "38" for mouse). Errors are specific: no internet, release not found (listing the latest releases), file not found in the release (listing the candidates), and failed or empty transfers (partial files are removed). Defaults: GENCODE release 50 (M39 for mouse), file_type = "gff", output_path = ":cache:".
  • group and levels choose the samples in the same way in every function that has them (productive_fraction(), productivity_fractions(), test_productive_fraction(), run_productivity_enrichment(), apa_usage(), test_apa(), profile_data(), plot_tx_expr(), dominant_isoform(), haplotype_summary(), test_usage(), de_confidence(), add_uncertainty(), prepare_profile_data()): samples of groups outside levels are ignored, as if the object had been subset to them, so a contrast between two of several groups needs no sub-object. The summary functions aborted in this case. Every returned value, including as_matrix = TRUE and the inferential standard deviations, comes from the samples kept. A level in levels without samples, or levels without group, is an error (isoformic_group_levels); samples without a group value are ignored with a message; factor levels without samples are not groups. dominant_isoform() and haplotype_summary() gain levels.
  • run_productivity_enrichment() gains rank_by = c("delta", "delta_z") to rank genes by the change in productive fraction divided by its standard deviation over the inferential replicates, and passes include_altered, min_expr and inf_reps on to productive_fraction(). The result has a rank_by column. delta_z is 0, not NA, for a gene whose productive fraction changes in no replicate; a change that is the same in every replicate is ranked with the largest delta_z.
  • productive_fraction() reads the inferential replicates one at a time and keeps only running sums, restricted to the transcripts of coding genes and the samples of the levels, instead of holding the fractions of all the replicates: about 14 times faster with about half the peak memory on 295,000 transcripts, 12 samples and 100 replicates, with the same results. inf_reps = FALSE skips the stored replicates. With the default rank_by = "delta", run_productivity_enrichment() does not read them.
  • run_productivity_enrichment() also takes the table of productive_fraction(), so that one table serves several gene set collections.
  • run_productivity_enrichment(rank_by = "statistic") ranks genes by the test of test_productive_fraction() on the "counts" assay, between the first and the last level, as the signed normal quantile of its p-value (the degrees of freedom differ between genes). It accounts for the reads of each gene and the variation between its samples, which delta_z, a measure of the quantification uncertainty only, does not. It also takes the table of test_productive_fraction().
  • productive_fraction(), test_productive_fraction() and run_productivity_enrichment() gain min_gene_count: genes whose mean count (the sum of their isoforms in the "counts" assay) is below it in any group are dropped before the statistics and the BH adjustment. Off by default (0).
  • add_uncertainty(), de_confidence(), inferential_overdispersion(), scale_counts(), uncertainty_report() and test_usage() read the inferential replicates one at a time from the stored list instead of copying them into a dense array: add_uncertainty(group = ) and de_confidence() held up to five arrays of the stored replicates at once and now hold one replicate at a time, with the same results.
  • run_enrichment() gains rank_by: besides the fold-change ("log2FC", the default) the transcripts can be ranked by -log10(pvalue) with the sign of the fold-change ("signed_p") or by the median fold-change over the inferential replicates divided by its standard deviation ("lfc_z", from the fold-change table of add_uncertainty(x, group = )), so that a fold-change the quantification cannot determine ranks low. The result has a rank_by column.
  • run_enrichment(), run_productivity_enrichment() and run_apa_enrichment() take several collections of gene sets at once (a named list of gene set lists, for example list(hallmark = read_gmt(h), reactome = read_gmt(r))): each collection is tested on its own and the result has a collection column, by which plot_enrichment() splits its panels. Every gene set and every collection now needs a name: a list with a missing or empty name is an error (isoformic_invalid_genesets) instead of a set dropped without notice. An enrichment without result is a table with the fgsea columns and no rows.
  • transcript_orfs() keeps the ORFs it computes in annot_data_orfs.parquet in the annotation directory, and later calls, sessions and objects with the same annotation read them back: for the 534,000 transcripts of GENCODE 49 the ORFs take 15 to 45 seconds instead of about 11 minutes, and transcript_productivity() about one minute instead of 10, once the table is written. The results are the same. options(isoformic.orf_cache = FALSE) turns the table off.
  • Computing ORFs and coding potential (transcript_orfs(), coding_potential(), and the productivity, polyadenylation and genomic context functions that use them) is about twice as fast, with the same results: the Fickett and hexamer scores are 3 to 7 times faster, and the coordinate conversions share one DuckDB connection.
  • cut_transcript_trees() reads the inferential replicates one at a time and keeps only the mean and variance of the tree nodes, instead of a dense array of all the replicates.
  • x[i, j] subsets everything stored by transcript or by sample: the inferential replicates in x@metadata$inf_reps and stored gene assays follow the assays, and the uncertainty tables are restricted to the kept transcripts. Dropping samples leaves the uncertainty tables as computed and says so (add_uncertainty(x) recomputes them from the subset replicates). Subscripts are checked (isoformic_invalid_subset), and must keep at least one transcript and one sample.
  • x[i, j] no longer copies the inferential replicates: the subset shares the draws of x and records its transcripts and samples in the selection attribute of metadata$inf_reps. Every function reads the draws through that selection, so the results are the same as before, and write_isoformic(), inferential_replicates_table() and inferential_moments_table() write or return only the selected transcripts and samples. A subset of a contrast of 6 samples no longer takes a copy of their draws (about 1.3 GB with 295,000 transcripts and 100 draws); in exchange, the draws of x stay in memory while the subset exists, and saveRDS() of a subset (or a copy sent to a parallel worker) carries them. Code that indexes metadata$inf_reps of a subset directly sees the draws of x, and so does a list operation such as lapply() or [, which drops the selection attribute: the functions that take the object still read only its kept transcripts and samples. inferential_replicates_table() and inferential_moments_table() take the object as a new x argument (alone, or with such a list as reps) to read the draws of its transcripts and samples in every case.
  • extract_transcript_sequences() warns when it keeps existing sequences (without overwrite = TRUE) that come from another source than the FASTA it is given, for example sequences of a cached annotation directory cut from a genome while a transcript FASTA is given, and says how many transcripts of the annotation have no sequence. The stored ORF tables of annotation directories are computed again on first use, because the ORF search changed.
  • test_usage() estimates the inferential overdispersion on the samples of the test, not on all the samples of the object.
  • The imported packages have minimum versions, those the package is developed and tested with: cli 3.6.6, DBI 1.3.0, dplyr 1.2.1, duckdb 1.5.4, fs 2.1.0, ggplot2 4.0.3, ggrepel 0.9.8, glue 1.8.1, rlang 1.3.0, S7 1.0.0, scales 1.4.0, tibble 3.3.1 and withr 3.0.3. The tests also pass with duckdb 2.0.0.
  • S7 1.0.0 is required. It stores a NULL property differently, which made IsoformicExperiment objects with no data_path fail validation under the earlier code. The package now uses the S7_on_load(), S7_on_unload() and S7_on_build() hooks of that release.
  • jsonlite and readr are in Suggests. The test that compares the inferential overdispersion with edgeR::catchSalmon() needs them.
  • Lower memory use and faster subsetting on large objects, with the same results. read_inferential_replicates() (and add_uncertainty(paths = )) holds one sample at a time instead of every sample twice, sums the replicates of a sample without copying them and frees each sample before the next one is read: on 12 placenta samples and GENCODE 50 (25 draws of 197,000 transcripts) its peak falls from about 3 to about 2.2 times the size of the replicates it returns, about 1.4 of which it keeps (the replicates and the moments of every transcript). x[i, j] matches the transcripts once instead of twice per replicate (about 3 times faster with 295,000 transcripts and 20 replicates), validates the object once, and returns the replicates without a copy when the subset keeps everything. A subset with other transcripts gets its own cache of derived tables, so it no longer replaces those of the object it came from. gene_assays(), as_isoformic() (IDs without |) and write_isoformic() no longer make spare copies of the assays.
  • Calls that need a few transcripts or genes of an annotation directory read only those, with the same results. transcript_sequences(transcript_id = ) (and so transcript_orfs() when it computes ORFs that are not stored yet) no longer loads every sequence: on GENCODE 50, 1,000 transcripts take 0.5 seconds and 740 MB instead of 8.5 seconds and 2.8 GB. prepare_exon_annotation(), exon_table() (when the exons of the object are not loaded yet) and transcript_features() and transcript_orfs() on a directory with gene_name read only the transcripts and exons of those genes: for six GENCODE 50 genes, 0.4 to 2.3 seconds and under 450 MB instead of 7 to 42 seconds and 1 to 3.6 GB; transcript_orfs() without a stored ORF table takes 1.2 seconds and about 700 MB instead of 4 minutes and 6 GB.
  • splice_site_strength() trains its position weight matrices once per annotation directory and session, and with gene_name reads and scores only the introns of those genes; on an IsoformicExperiment the table by transcript is cached in the object. The scores are the same. On GENCODE 50, one gene takes 9.5 s and 590 MB the first time and the next gene 0.3 s, instead of 115 s and 2.3 GB each, and the genome-wide table by transcript takes 39 s and 1.3 GB instead of 115 s and 2.2 GB.
  • poison_exons() reads only the exons of the transcripts it looks at (when the exon table is not loaded yet) and lists the transcripts of the candidate exons only, with the same results: 177,000 transcripts of GENCODE 50 take 4 s and 560 MB instead of 30 s and 1.2 GB.
  • transcript_features() and splicing_events() compare each transcript with the canonical isoform of its gene using integer keys and a single overlap join, with the same results. On all of GENCODE 50 the splicing events step peaks at 1.4 GB instead of 2.5 GB, and the whole of transcript_features() at 2.1 GB instead of 3.3 GB; options(isoformic.duckdb_threads = 4) lowers that step to 1 GB.
  • prepare_isoformic_annotation() extracts the gene and transcript attributes only from the gene and transcript features, and from the exons and CDS only their transcript, exon ID and number, with the same tables. The comprehensive GENCODE 50 annotation with patches and haplotypes converts in 29 seconds with a peak of 2.1 GB, instead of 90 seconds and 5.0 GB (GFF3), or in 41 seconds with a peak of 3.2 GB instead of 105 seconds and 5.1 GB (GTF), with four DuckDB threads.
  • merge_annotations() copies each table from the Parquet files of the haplotypes to the merged file in DuckDB instead of reading them into R, with the same tables, and copies the transcript sequences with one DuckDB thread. Merging two GENCODE 50 annotations with their transcript sequences takes 10 seconds and 1.8 GB instead of 54 seconds and 4.7 GB.
  • add_uncertainty() keeps the cached derived tables of the object (such as those of transcript_features() and transcript_productivity()), which do not depend on the uncertainty tables, instead of discarding them, so they are not recomputed after it (about 50 seconds for the features of 295,000 transcripts). It no longer empties the cache of the object it was given either.
  • as_summarized_experiment() leaves the inferential replicates out of the metadata of the result.
  • All the bundled examples (example_isoformic(), example.gff3.gz, example_transcripts.fa.gz, mini_quants/, oarfish/, oarfish_sc/), the ESRP knockdown examples, the placenta tables of the articles and the case-study bundles are rebuilt on GENCODE 50 (mouse M39), with Salmon 2.8.0 and Oarfish 0.10.3 (the case studies with Salmon 2.11.0 and Oarfish 0.11.0), from scripts now tracked in data-raw/ (placenta/, knockdown/, case_studies/, oarfish/, with prepare_extdata.R and build_knockdown_example.R).
  • The mini example (mini_quants/, mini_draws.parquet, mini_annotation/) now holds three preeclampsia (SRR11498039 to SRR11498041) and three control placentas (SRR11498077 to SRR11498079), quantified against the transcripts of 15 genes with 20 Gibbs draws, instead of SRR11498039 to SRR11498041 and SRR11498079 to SRR11498081, so the examples compare preeclampsia with control.
  • The identifiers of the bundled examples changed with the release: code that hardcodes GENCODE v33 transcript or gene IDs of the example experiment, example.gff3.gz or example_transcripts.fa.gz (or v49 IDs of mini_annotation/) must be updated to their GENCODE 50 versions.

Fixed

  • add_uncertainty(paths = ) on an object without a counts assay reads the replicates of the object’s transcripts only. It read every transcript of the quantification, so the tables recomputed from the stored replicates and the replicates written by write_isoformic() covered fewer transcripts than the tables built from paths.
  • download_reference() uses a file already in output_path without contacting the server when the request determines its name (GENCODE annotations, transcript and poly(A) files, MANE with an explicit version, FANTOM CAT), so a cached reference works offline and no longer fails on a transient error listing the release directory. For the other requests (GENCODE genomes, Ensembl annotations of an explicit release, NCBI and T2T assemblies), when the listing fails and exactly one cached file matches, that file is used with a message: a GENCODE genome must be of the release’s assembly (GRCh37 up to release 19, GRCm38 up to M25), and an Ensembl region = "all" annotation must be the chr_patch_hapl_scaff file. Requests for the current Ensembl or MANE release still need the listing.
  • example_isoformic() copies the bundled annotation directory to a new temporary directory on every call and points the object there, so the functions that store tables in the annotation (extract_transcript_sequences(), transcript_orfs(), add_appris(), add_riboseq_orfs(), add_nmd_exons()) no longer write into, or fail on, the installed package. write_isoformic() copies an annotation directory that lies under tempdir() into an experiment directory written outside tempdir() (with a message), so an experiment saved from example_isoformic() can be read in a later session; before, it pointed at a directory removed when the session ended.
  • salmon_index(decoy_fasta = ) builds a decoy-aware index (usually with the genome FASTA of the same release, plain or compressed with gzip, xz or bzip2): it writes the gentrome (transcripts followed by the decoys) and decoys.txt to a temporary directory and passes them to salmon index. The argument was accepted and ignored before. A decoy compressed with xz or bzip2, or with CRLF line endings anywhere in the file (plain or gzipped), is decompressed line by line instead of being appended as raw bytes, and decoy names that are also transcript names are an error.
  • Subsetting an object to transcripts that have no stored inferential replicates (those below min_count in add_uncertainty()) keeps the replicate moments, so scale_counts() and inferential_overdispersion() still work on the subset. The draws themselves are not kept (zero-row draws), and the functions that need them treat the subset as an object without inferential replicates.
  • test_usage(method = "DEXSeq") no longer prints the DESeq2 note about the dispersion trend fit.
  • The Salmon and Terminus environments are created without the deprecation warning of the packages argument of condathis::create_env(): the package spec is passed unnamed, which every condathis version accepts.
  • The ... argument of the generics whose methods do not use it is documented as not used.
  • Fixes from a code review: write_isoformic(overwrite = TRUE) writes to a sibling directory and swaps it in, so overwriting the directory an object was read from no longer deletes it (and refuses directories that are not experiments, isoformic_not_experiment_dir); de_table() and plot_log2fc() accept results that already have gene_name, gene_id or transcript_name columns; test_productive_fraction() and test_apa() contrast two of several groups with levels; join_DEG_DET() uses the same cutoff rule as the stored cutoffs (>= and <=) and gains use_fdr; a frozen dataset that fails its checksum after download is discarded and the next mirror is tried; plot_log2fc() no longer drops its title when a requested feature has no data; the assay hash behind the caches is computed once when the assays are set; tools is declared in Imports.
  • productive_fraction() with inferential replicates stops when a level of group is named sd, whose column productive_fraction_sd used to be overwritten by the standard deviation over the replicates.
  • productive_fraction_sd of productive_fraction() is now the standard deviation of each gene’s productive fraction over the inferential replicates, around their mean, averaged over the samples. It was the root mean square distance of the draws to the fraction of the assay, which also counted the gap between the mean of Gibbs draws and the EM estimate, and, with the default assay = "abundance", compared fractions of TPM with fractions of the counts the draws hold. The draws are now put on the scale of assay first (multiplied by assay / counts of each transcript and sample; where a count is zero, from the length assay or a fit over the other transcripts and samples, see ?productivity), so delta_productive_fraction_sd, delta_z and rank_by = "delta_z" of run_productivity_enrichment() compare TPM changes with TPM spread, and min_expr applies on one scale. The draws are taken to be counts, as read_inferential_replicates() returns them: draws on another scale given to an object with a counts assay are rescaled too, while an object without one uses them as they are. The spread counts only the samples where the assay gives the gene a fraction. Expect smaller productive_fraction_sd values: on 25 placenta samples with 30 Gibbs draws (GENCODE 50, chromosome 1), the old value was a median 2.2 times the new one (90% quantile 5.2 times), 1.9 times with assay = "counts". The median delta_productive_fraction_sd with assay = "abundance" rises from 0.017 to 0.023, so fewer genes reach abs(delta_z) >= 1.96 (697 instead of 813 of 2,064 genes; Spearman correlation of delta_z before and after 0.985); with assay = "counts" it barely changes (677 instead of 679).
  • productive_fraction(gene_name = ) and min_gene_count keep only the genes asked for before summing the assay and each inferential replicate, with the same results: one gene of chromosome 1 with 30 draws takes 0.14 s and about 60 MB instead of 0.6 s and 410 MB.
  • write_isoformic(copy_annotation = TRUE) does not copy the stored ORF table, which was not valid for the copy.
  • prepare_isoformic_annotation() kept only the first ##sequence-region of a GENCODE GFF3 file (one row, chr1), because GENCODE writes one pragma before the features of each sequence and only the header was read. The whole file is now scanned (annot_seq_regions.parquet has 706 rows for GENCODE 50 chr_patch_hapl_scaff), and a sequence without a pragma keeps the largest feature end. Annotation directories made before this fix hold the single row: rebuild them with overwrite = TRUE if you use the table.
  • The inferential relative variance (mean_inf_rv, max_inf_rv, group_inf_rv of cut_transcript_trees()) now is the formula of fishpond::computeInfRV(), max(var - mean, 0) / (mean + 5) + 0.01, as the documentation said. It was max(0.01, var - mean) / (mean + 5): about 0.01 lower, and far below 0.01 for transcripts whose draws vary no more than counts. A transcript within 0.01 below inf_rv_cutoff is now uncertain. The tables of the uncertainty and stability articles were rebuilt.
  • The source files of the frozen datasets are cached per dataset version (get_isoformic_cache("sources", <name>, <version>)). With one directory per dataset, a new version in the registry reused the cached file of the old one, which has the same name, and rebuilt the old data.
  • x[, j] no longer fails on an object with stored gene assays, and a factor subscript is read as IDs, not as its integer codes.
  • dominant_isoform() and haplotype_summary() failed with a single group.
  • de_confidence(collapse_groups = TRUE) labelled a transcript with the ID of its ambiguity group when it was the only member left in the object.
  • isoform_fraction() returned cached fractions after gene_assays<-.
  • Stored gene assays whose columns are in another order than the transcript assays gave wrong fractions in isoform_fraction(), dominant_isoform() and profile_data(); the matrices are now matched by sample ID.
  • run_enrichment() and run_productivity_enrichment() run fgsea with BiocParallel::SerialParam() unless BPPARAM or nproc is given; the default socket cluster failed (serialize() errors) or hung on Windows (#9).
  • extract_transcript_sequences() and extract_splice_sites() drop the carriage returns of Windows (CRLF) FASTA files.
  • DuckDB connections set their extension, secret and temporary directories under the session temporary directory, which silences the storage warnings of DuckDB 2.0.
  • build_frozen_nmd_exons() no longer replaces the Ensembl gene_id with the StringTie GeneID of the source table.
  • The default tests, examples and site build use only the bundled data; everything that downloads references or runs external tools runs only with ISOFORMIC_FULL=true.
  • test_productive_fraction() and test_apa() no longer test genes with fewer than 5 reads in their smaller class (productive or not, distal or not), pooled over both groups, or without reads in one group. The continuity correction gave such genes, including those with a stray fraction of a read in one class, a log odds ratio of about the log fold-change of the gene: a change in expression, not in usage. They have no statistic or p-value and do not enter the BH adjustment; their log odds ratio is 0, or NA without reads in one group.
  • DuckDB queries that spill to disk (under a memory limit set by the isoformic.duckdb_memory_limit option, Slurm or a cgroup) no longer fail because the spill directory could not be created.
  • run_enrichment() on an object whose stored transcript results already have transcript_type, transcript_name or gene_name columns takes them from the annotation instead of failing.
  • as_inferential_replicates() and the moments table it reads reject a table where one transcript and sample (and draw) has two rows, instead of silently leaving the missing cell at zero.

Removed

  • assay(), assays() and assay<-, renamed to tx_assay(), tx_assays() and tx_assay<- (see Changed).
  • ContextData and create_context_data().
  • Imported packages forcats, GenomicFeatures, ggpubr, IRanges, plotgardener, purrr, stringr, tidyr, txdbmaker and vroom; fgsea and readr move to Suggests. Suggested packages rmarkdown and viridis.
  • The isoformic_intro vignette, replaced by the articles of the documentation site.
  • The example files of 0.1.2 under extdata (DEGs_PE_fixed2.csv, DETs_fixed.csv, PE_1_DETs.csv, PE_1_counts.csv, hsapiens_REAC_subset.gmt and the complete MSigDB Reactome collection c2.cp.reactome.v2023.1.Hs.symbols.gmt.txt), to keep the package small. reactome_subset.gmt replaces the gene set subset; the complete placenta tables and the Reactome collection that the articles use are in the source repository, under vignettes/articles/data/preeclampsia/.

Isoformic 0.1.2

  • New tx_type_palette() function to provide a default color palette for transcript types.

Fixed

  • In make_tx_to_gene() output, wrong column name entrez_id replaced for tx_length.

Fixed
